rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A deed becomes a crime before God when a person commits it deliberately while knowing it is wrong.
rows.anchor: an act becomes a crime in the eyes of God when it is done intentionally after knowing that it is wrong

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wealth and children become a trial when attachment to them makes a person neglect duties owed to God, who bestowed them.
rows.anchor: When the love of wealth and children prevails on a person to the extent that he begins to shirk responsibilities

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Excessive love of wealth and children underlies insincerity toward God and His Messenger and neglected duties to others, making it a major door to hypocrisy.
rows.anchor: It is the over-blown love of wealth and children that lies at the base of insincerity with God and His messenger

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To withstand this trial, believers should remember the great reward and prefer God's and His Messenger's pleasure whenever it conflicts with family or wealth.
rows.anchor: if there is a clash at some instance between earning the pleasure of God and His messenger and between love for wealth and children

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The section first encourages believers to honor their covenant without yielding to attachment to wealth and children, promising that God will manifest the furqān and remove veils from truth.
rows.anchor: resolutely abide by their promise with God and not show weakness by being overcome with the love for wealth and children

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's scheme saves the Messenger from the disbelievers' united conspiracy and opens the way for migration, which becomes a decisive step in truth's contest with evil and Islam's ascendancy.
rows.anchor: the effective scheme of God is referred to which He employed

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quraysh mocked the Qur'an and demanded punishment, but God does not punish a people while their Messenger remains among them; migration removes that restraint.
rows.anchor: as along as a Messenger remains among his people, God does not send any punishment to them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers arrogantly claim their efforts established God's religion and that they are its custodians while performing rites.
rows.anchor: They think that it is because of their efforts that God’s religion is rooted in the society

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers' spending to obstruct God's religion will become a source of regret; they will be defeated here and gathered for Hell in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: They will be defeated in this world and in the Hereafter God will gather them and throw them into Hell

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quraysh should change course and accept the Prophet's message, or remember the fate of earlier peoples who denied their messengers.
rows.anchor: it is better if they change their ways and accept the Prophet’s message; otherwise, they should remember

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers are instructed to keep fighting until persecution ends and God's religion alone remains in the land; God will support them.
rows.anchor: continue to wage war against them until the persecution they are guilty of is done away with and no religion except that of God remains in the land

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Furqān means anything that distinguishes good from evil, whether internal or external, intellectual or ideological, or an event or practical occurrence.
rows.anchor: “ Furqān” means everything which distinguishes good from evil. This distinguishing thing can be internal as well as external

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an uses furqān for proofs and arguments, and this sūrah calls Badr furqān because it showed who was right and wrong; the Qur'an and Torah use the term similarly.
rows.anchor: the Qur’ ān also regards proofs and arguments to be “ furqān” because through them it distinguishes good from evil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If believers remain God-fearing and sincere, God will make truth prevail and clear the present doubts; contextual signs identify this furqān as Islam's dominance.
rows.anchor: here the word “ furqān” is referring to the dominance of Islam and the Muslims

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although Badr had already provided one furqān, evil forces still surrounded the believers; the verse addresses Muslims whose doubt and reluctance produced the weaknesses discussed earlier.
rows.anchor: The verse actually addresses such reluctant Muslims

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word siyāt denotes minor sins to which humans are prone; if people avoid major sins, God will not hold them to account for minor ones, for He is gracious.
rows.anchor: refers to minor sins which people are prone to as human beings

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Athbāt literally means stopping or restricting someone and can include imprisoning them.
rows.anchor: which also includes “to imprison someone.”

rows.speaker: Quraysh leaders
rows.claim: At Dār al-Nadwah, leaders proposed different plans, but the historical and biographical accounts indicate they chose to kill the Prophet with every clan participating to forestall qiṣāṣ against his family.
rows.anchor: after discussion the suggestion to kill him was adopted

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's being the best schemer means His plan prevails and apparent enemy victories ultimately open routes for truth's victory, as the migration illustrates.
rows.anchor: His scheme always prevails on others

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The migration let Islam spread in Madīnah, while the Quraysh who thought the Prophet's departure would end his message could only await events helplessly.
rows.anchor: this departure became the prelude to the widespread dissemination of Islam in the free environment of Madīnah

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reminding believers of the conspiracy reinforces the preceding promise of furqān: the Prophet's escape and migration testify that God turns hostile circumstances into eventual success.
rows.anchor: the purpose of reminding the believers of this promise was to reinforce the promise of manifestation of the “ furqān” mentioned in the previous verse

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God can turn enemies into agents of truth's victory; believers should trust the best of schemers rather than fear adverse circumstances, since truth will emerge as furqān.
rows.anchor: Whenever He intends, He uses the enemies to accomplish the very task of reaping victory for the truth and destroying the enemy

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verse 30 both continues the prior promise of furqān and introduces the next warning: the Quraysh were spared while the Prophet remained among them, but his migration removes their immunity; direct address honors and consoles him.
rows.anchor: In one aspect, it is connected with the previous topic and in the other it is a prelude to a forthcoming topic

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quraysh's boasts that they could produce similar revelation and their demand for punishment arose amid repeated challenges and harassment; continued respite made them more arrogant about their falsehood.
rows.anchor: the Quraysh would continuously challenge God to send punishment and would also arrogantly harass the Prophet

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is addressed directly to express special affection for him while answering the Quraysh's demand for punishment.
rows.anchor: specially show affection to the Prophet (sws), he is directly addressed

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Messenger among his people is like their heart: his appeal for forgiveness and invitation to repent shield them; even after migration, seeking forgiveness can still save the people, while calamities before departure serve only as warnings, not decisive punishment.
rows.anchor: as long as a Messenger is present among his people, he is like their heart

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After a nation plots to kill its Messenger and righteous people suffer, migration removes its immunity; if few believe, a natural disaster wipes the nation away, since evil's flourishing opposes the universe's nature and its Creator's wisdom.
rows.anchor: if only a few people profess faith in the messenger, the nation is punished directly by God through some natural disaster

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When a substantial number believe, as with Muhammad, conflict follows and truth ultimately vanquishes evil, as stated in 17:81.
rows.anchor: A conflict ensues between the righteous and the wrongdoers. Ultimately, evil is totally decimated and vanquished by the truth

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rhetorical question asking what eminence the Quraysh possess severely criticizes their arrogance in treating custody of the House and rituals as grounds to presume divine favor; the author compares this delusion with that of Jews, Christians, and the present ummah.
rows.anchor: what eminence do they have that God should not punish them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quraysh believed their Abrahamic descent and services to pilgrims made them God's favorites, so prophetic warnings felt intolerable to them and they imagined the House protected them.
rows.anchor: The Quraysh thought that they were the progeny of Abraham (sws)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quraysh blocked Muslims, whom the author identifies as Abraham's true adherents seeking to purify the House from polytheism, from entering the sanctuary and even expelled them from Makkah.
rows.anchor: They are the ones who are the real adherents to the religion of Abraham (sws) and want to once again cleanse it from polytheism

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because they betrayed the House's purpose and violated its sanctity, the Quraysh have no right to its custody and should not expect God to protect them on that basis.
rows.anchor: These words also indicate that these people are dishonest, they are traitors and have violated the sanctity of this House

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's leadership promise applied only to the righteous among his descendants; since the House was its center, its custodians and heirs to that leadership must uphold monotheism, its limits, and its covenant.
rows.anchor: His promise was for the righteous among it and not for its wrongdoers

rows.speaker: Jesus (sws)
rows.claim: Jesus told Jewish scholars claiming custody of Bayt al-Maqdis that God's house should be a house of prayer, while they had made it a den of robbers.
rows.anchor: My house will be called a house of prayer, but you are making it a den of robbers

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Arabs' ignorance meant they retained pride in Abrahamic lineage but forgot Abraham's mission, the House's purpose, the Ishmaelites' trusts, and the meaning of its custodianship.
rows.anchor: They did remember out of familial superiority that they were the progeny of Abraham (sws) and Ishmael (sws). Yet beyond this

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inherited family control of the House and altered Hajj rites made it a national shrine; the Qur'an exposes the custodians' ignorance of the House's status and the duties of its keepers.
rows.anchor: They would take pride in this and in this capacity of theirs administer the House of God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their whistling and clapping show they neither merit custody nor understand the House's purpose; Abraham's prayer and the House's intended worship are explained elsewhere, including 14:35-37.
rows.anchor: neither are these people worthy of being the custodians of the House of God nor do they have any knowledge of the purpose for which it was built

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham settled Ishmael's descendants near the House so they would establish prayer; the Quraysh later turned the House to idolatry and violated the prayer's very purpose.
rows.anchor: was the ritual of the prayer

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quraysh's clapping and whistling are jesting, not prayer; outward and inward criteria let religiously insightful people recognize innovations that cannot belong to religion.
rows.anchor: how can such jesting have anything to do with the prayer

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says Shiite mourning rites, shrine practices, and Sufi gatherings visibly lack religion's dignity and purity, and that spiritual insight can expose them before formal research.
rows.anchor: mourning rites among Shiites and irreligious practices at shrines

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: True religious practice reflects dignity, decency, humility, purity, wisdom, sagacity, and spirituality; outwardly the custodians' ritual is satanic and unlike Abraham's prayer.
rows.anchor: Every aspect of religion has the reflection of dignity, decency, humility and purity

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mouth sounds, whistling, and instrumental music belong to one category associated with idolatrous worship; their possible use to scare devils or ghosts is only conjecture.
rows.anchor: whistling and playing music from an instrument all belong to the same category

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whistling, mouth sounds, and instrumental music appear in idolatrous worship; the author speculates that the sounds may have been used to scare away devils or ghosts.
rows.anchor: It may be that these things were used to scare away devils and ghosts

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whistling, mouth sounds, and instrumental music belong to idolatrous rites; the Quraysh placed tribal idols at the House to assert religious leadership, and Abraham's prayer was displaced until only clapping and whistling remained.
rows.anchor: Ultimately, matters reached the extent that the prayer prescribed by Abraham (sws) was no longer offered in the House of God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage shifts from an indirect question about punishment to direct address, warning the Quraysh after listing their crimes; it threatens further reversals after Badr and rebukes their false pride in custody.
rows.anchor: The first verse: “and why should He not punish them” began without address anyone directly. The last part of the second verse

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At Badr the Quraysh lavishly funded provisions, with chiefs competing to contribute; their arms and abundant spending intimidated weaker Muslims, who doubted their own scant resources.
rows.anchor: at the time of the battle of Badr, the Quraysh had generously spent on the provisions of the battle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers should not be intimidated by the Quraysh's spending: it cannot stop truth's advance and will instead end in their humiliation and defeat in both worlds.
rows.anchor: Their efforts to stop the truth from manifesting itself will not succeed

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition عَلَى with yuḥshar adds the sense of driving to the verb.
rows.anchor: This has incorporated the meaning of “driving” in the verb

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The furqān in the Hereafter is God's separation of good from evil; rakm means piling in layers, and the layered heap burns intensely, subtly depicting disbelievers who aided each other becoming fuel for one another.
rows.anchor: The word رﻛﻢmeans to gather something in layers atop each other

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The losers lose in both lives: their worldly spending earns no reward and brings regret and defeat, while in the Hereafter they are cast into Hell like a heap of filth.
rows.anchor: In this world, they will end up earning no reward for their spending and thereby regret it

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quraysh are invited to avert doom by stopping their hostility, repenting, reforming, and accepting the Prophet; God will forgive their past and not punish them.
rows.anchor: they should abstain from this attitude, repent, mend their ways and accept the message of the Prophet

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning immediately follows the invitation: if the Quraysh repeat their hostility, the divine precedent for earlier peoples applies to them.
rows.anchor: The words “and if they repeat it, then the practice of God for the previous people has passed” is a sentence of warning right after they were exhorted
